newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMRAD agrees to A$20 mln share buy-back.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMRAD agrees to A$20 mln share buy-back.

text.p: Biomedical research company AMRAD Corp Ltd has agreed to buy back 10 million shares for A$20 million from its biggest shareholder, the Victoria state government, state Treasurer Alan Stockdale said on Wednesday.
The buy-back will be carried out as part of the company's initial public offering and float on the Australian Stock Exchange in December, Stockdale said in a statement.
The buy-back is based on AMRAD's application price of A$1.95 per share and follows the government's move in 1993 to reduce its shareholding to 35.5 percent from 58 percent.

"The share buy-back is another step in the government's previously announced strategic reduction of its interest in AMRAD, which is moving to a new phase as a publicly listed company on the Australian Stock Exchange," Stockdale said.
The buy-back will leave the government with about 20 million shares, or around 16 percent of the company after listing.
The offer of 36 million new shares in the company aims to raise A$70 million.
The proceeds will be used to fund the buy-back and in the research and development of new drugs, AMRAD said in a separate statement on Wednesday.
The issue opened on Tuesday and closes on November 20.
